_about.what: The shape of one state object in src/content/certs/motorcycle-endorsement-facts.json, with 'what' and 'why' standing in for the 'value' and 'source' of a real fact. Not read by any code.
_about.why: One place that says what each field is for, how we prefer to fill it, and every value a constrained field is allowed to take. Zod will enforce the shape later; this explains it, which Zod never will.
_about.purpose: These facts feed auto-generated quick-facts content whose job is to give a rider the headline answer and send them to the primary source for the detail. Every value must be honest and traceable to a document we hold. It does not have to carry every edge case — copy hedges and links out, and a fact that tries to be exhaustive stops being quick. Record the headline answer; put a genuinely load-bearing exception in meta.note and leave the rest to the source.
_about.factContract: Every fact is a { value, source } pair. 'source' is a key into motorcycle-endorsement-sources.json. A fact is verified if and only if it has a source: source null means not researched, and a source present with value null means checked and there is no single honest answer for this state.
_about.valueTypes: number | string | boolean | [min, max]. A range is exactly two numbers, ascending, in the same unit — used where the honest answer varies by county or provider.
_about.newValues: A constrained field that needs a value not listed here stays null and becomes an end-of-run question. Never invent a vocabulary entry mid-run.

dateVerified.what: Date every fact in this state object was last verified, as YYYY-MM-DD.
dateVerified.why: The visible trust signal on the state page, and what the 60-day revalidation sweep reads. Bumped only when the whole state was re-checked in one pass — a partial pass leaves it alone, or the date starts vouching for facts nobody looked at.

dmvCode.what: Short agency abbreviation as it appears in body copy — FLHSMV, GA DDS.
dmvCode.why: Lives here rather than in states.json because the agency is cert-family-specific: the same agency serves motorcycle and CDL, but hunter ed would be a different one.

dmvName.what: The agency's full name, spelled out.
dmvName.why: Used on first mention and in structured data; dmvCode carries every mention after.

localTerm.what: What this state actually calls the credential — Florida 'motorcycle endorsement', Georgia 'Class M license'.
localTerm.why: The national term is simply wrong in some states. The cert's name is the default and this overrides it, so copy can use the phrase a rider will recognize.

note.what: Internal only. Bare facts about this state that no field can hold.
note.why: For us, not for readers. Facts only — no caveats, no rationale, no explanation of why a field is null, nothing too minor to matter. If it needs a sentence of justification, it is not a note.

stateDetails.what: User-facing prose explaining this state's quirks on its own page. Null until written.
stateDetails.why: The piece that lets every other field stay cookie-cutter while each state page still earns its own SEO.

questionCount.what: Number of questions on the knowledge exam.
questionCount.why: Where a state administers no test of its own, this describes the knowledge test inside the required course, and meta.note has to say so — otherwise the page implies a DMV exam that does not exist.

timeLimitMinutes.what: Minutes allowed for the knowledge exam.
timeLimitMinutes.why: Frequently unpublished. When an agency genuinely states no limit, the honest record is value null with a source attached, not an unresearched null.

passingScorePercent.what: Percentage of questions that must be correct to pass.
passingScorePercent.why: Cannot express a per-section gate on its own — see isExamSectioned before recording one for a split exam.

isExamSectioned.what: Whether the knowledge exam is split into separately scored sections.
isExamSectioned.why: A holding field, deliberately. Georgia's exam is two 20-question sections each needing 15 correct, which questionCount 40 plus passingScorePercent 75 flattens into a score that passes a rider who failed. This flags the case so exam mode never scores one wrong; the real section model gets designed once several states' segmentation is known rather than guessed now. When true, meta.note records the segmentation as bare facts.

values.true: Scored in two or more parts, each with its own gate.
values.false: One undivided test with a single passing score.

dmvCost.what: Total the rider pays the agency for the credential, in USD.
dmvCost.why: A single number where the state charges one, a [min, max] range where it varies by county or office. The registry note records what the figure is composed of, since a total assembled from three line items is not checkable without it.

classCost.what: What the rider course costs, in USD.
classCost.why: Usually a range, because providers set their own tuition. Where the number is a survey of rates published by the providers an agency directory lists — rather than a figure the agency prints — the registry note must say so, or the next revalidation hunts for a line that was never there.

minAge.what: Youngest age at which the credential itself can be obtained.
minAge.why: The credential, not the learner permit. A state offering a permit at 16 and the license at 17 records 17; the permit age is a meta.note fact.

minLicense.what: What a rider must already hold before pursuing this credential.
minLicense.why: Constrained rather than free text so the state page can branch on it.

values.Learners: A learner or instruction permit is required first.
values.Drivers: A full, already-issued driver license is required first. Deliberately generic — states name the same credential differently (Florida Class E, Georgia Class C), and localTerm is where state naming lives.

transferOutOfStateEndorsement.what: Whose existing motorcycle credential this state accepts in place of retesting.
transferOutOfStateEndorsement.why: Constrained so the UI can branch. Note the shape is already strained: a value naming one specific state does not scale, and a third exclusion pattern is the signal that this field wants to become a list rather than a token.

values.all: Accepts a valid motorcycle credential from every other US jurisdiction.
values.none: Accepts no out-of-state credential in place of retesting. Every applicant tests in-state regardless of what they hold elsewhere — California is the case.
values.non-Alabama: Accepts every other US jurisdiction outright. An Alabama credential is accepted only when presented with an MSF Basic RiderCourse completion card — the token names the exception, and copy carries the condition.

courseType.what: The rider-training curriculum this state's course is built on.
courseType.why: Load-bearing beyond display: a question's applies_to resolves a course type against this field at build time to reach every state running that curriculum. Verify it rather than assuming — California runs CMSP, and several states run programs that are MSF-derived but distinct, so a wrong value here silently scopes content to the wrong states.

values.MNS2011: Any curriculum the state approved against the 2011 Model National Standards for Entry-Level Motorcycle Rider Training (USDOT/NHTSA). Used where the state regulates to a standard instead of naming a curriculum, so several conformant curricula — MSF's among them — may be in use at once. Deliberately not MSFBRC: a rider's school may have taught something else.
values.CA: California's own curriculum, delivered by the CMSP under CHP contract. Naming convention: a curriculum belonging to exactly one state takes that state's code, and only curricula spanning states get a broad name like MSFBRC. Keeps question assignment legible — a broad token means a group worth authoring for, a state code means content that travels nowhere else.

findCourse.what: How a rider finds and books a course.
findCourse.why: Decides which call to action the state page shows. Lives in criteria despite not being a criterion, so all the fact objects stay grouped.

values.stateLocator: The agency publishes a directory of independent providers and the rider contacts one directly.
values.stateProgram: The agency runs a single booking portal covering all courses.

requirementType.what: What kind of machine triggers the requirement for this credential.
requirementType.why: Constrained because it decides who the page is even for — a rider on a 49cc scooter needs a different answer than one on a 650.

values.50ccUp: Required for any motorcycle above 50cc; 50cc and under is treated as a moped.
values.all: Required at every engine size, with no moped exemption. California is the case: a moped or motorized bicycle needs a Class M2 and a motorcycle needs an M1, so there is no unlicensed tier at all.

expirationType.what: How long the credential lasts before it must be renewed.
expirationType.why: A token rather than a number so that 'never' and a fixed term can share one field. New terms follow the same form.

values.never: Does not expire on its own.

additionalResources.what: An array of registry keys for user-facing links that no fact already cites.
additionalResources.why: The 'Verified against' list is derived from the source fields, so this holds only what would otherwise never appear on the page. Never repeat a key already used as a source — the two render as separate lists and a duplicate shows up twice.
